title: Lock it down
briefing: secrets.conf is readable by everyone on the machine. Make it yours alone.
tips: `chmod 600 file` = owner may read+write, nobody else anything. (6 = rw, 0 = nothing.)
objective: Change ~/secrets.conf so only its owner can read and write it — no access for group or others.
hints: You want rw for you, nothing for group or others. In octal that's three digits.
read=4 write=2 execute=1. Owner rw = 6, group 0, others 0 -> 600.
explanation: Each octal digit is read(4)+write(2)+execute(1), for owner/group/others. 600 = rw-------, 644 = rw-r--r--, 755 = rwxr-xr-x. Secrets should be 600; the world does not need to read your passwords.
